system: AURA Medical Emergency and Disease Prediction Knowledge Base
disclaimer: AURA provides evidence-based clinical risk estimates and triage support for educational and emergency response purposes. It does not replace professional medical diagnosis, laboratory testing, or physician consultation.

diseases.name: Hypothyroidism
diseases.definition: A clinical syndrome resulting from deficiency of thyroid hormones (thyroxine T4 and triiodothyronine T3), leading to generalized metabolic slowing.

clinical_thresholds.source: American Thyroid Association (ATA) / European Thyroid Association (ETA)
clinical_thresholds.clinical_note: Elevated TSH with subnormal Free T4 defines overt primary hypothyroidism.

common_symptoms: Chronic fatigue and lethargy
Cold intolerance
Unexplained weight gain
Constipation
Dry skin and coarse, thinning hair
Bradycardia (low heart rate)
Depression and cognitive slowing ('brain fog')
risk_factors: Female sex (5-8x higher prevalence)
Age > 60 years
Personal or family history of autoimmune disorders (e.g., Hashimoto's thyroiditis, Type 1 Diabetes)
Prior thyroid surgery or radioiodine therapy
Postpartum status
emergency_red_flags: Myxedema coma: severe hypothermia, marked bradycardia, altered mental status, hypoventilation, hypotension
Immediate emergency dispatch (112 / 108 / 911) required if unresponsiveness or stupor occurs.
clinical_management: First-line replacement therapy: Levothyroxine (LT4) oral administration
Target TSH normalization between 0.5 and 2.5 mIU/L in young adults
Routine re-testing every 6 to 12 weeks during dose titration

diseases.name: Hyperthyroidism
diseases.definition: A hypermetabolic clinical state resulting from excessive production and secretion of thyroid hormones by the thyroid gland (most commonly Graves' disease or toxic multinodular goitre).

clinical_thresholds.clinical_note: Suppressed TSH with elevated Free T4 / Free T3 defines overt thyrotoxicosis.

common_symptoms: Palpitations and tachycardia (resting heart rate > 100 bpm)
Unexplained weight loss despite increased appetite
Heat intolerance and profuse sweating
Tremor in hands and fingers
Anxiety, irritability, and insomnia
Frequent bowel movements or diarrhea
Exophthalmos (bulging eyes in Graves' disease)
risk_factors: Female sex
Graves' disease autoimmune history
High dietary iodine or amiodarone medication
Family history of thyroid storm or thyrotoxicosis
emergency_red_flags: Thyroid Storm: life-threatening hyperpyrexia (> 40°C / 104°F), extreme tachycardia, atrial fibrillation, delirium, cardiovascular collapse
clinical_management: Antithyroid medications: Methimazole or Propylthiouracil (PTU)
Beta-blockers (e.g., Propranolol) for acute symptomatic rate control
Definitive options: Radioactive Iodine (I-131) ablation or thyroidectomy

diseases.name: Subclinical Thyroid Dysfunction
diseases.definition: An asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic biochemical state characterized by abnormal serum TSH concentrations accompanied by circulating Free T4 and Free T3 within reference ranges.

clinical_thresholds.source: American Thyroid Association / ETA Consensus Guidelines
clinical_thresholds.subclinical_hypo: TSH > 4.5 mIU/L AND FT4 between 0.8 - 1.8 ng/dL
clinical_thresholds.subclinical_hyper: TSH < 0.4 mIU/L AND FT4 between 0.8 - 1.8 ng/dL
clinical_thresholds.clinical_note: Requires confirmatory repeat panel in 2-3 months before initiating pharmacotherapy.

common_symptoms: Mild fatigue or subclinical mood changes
Subtle lipid profile abnormalities (mild hypercholesterolemia)
Often completely asymptomatic and detected on routine wellness screens
risk_factors: Advanced age (> 65 years)
Positive anti-TPO (thyroid peroxidase) autoantibodies
History of neck radiation therapy
emergency_red_flags: Progression to overt failure or precipitation into arrhythmia if untreated with severe cardiovascular comorbidities
clinical_management: Watchful surveillance with serial TSH/FT4 every 3-6 months
Consider low-dose levothyroxine if TSH > 10 mIU/L or high cardiovascular risk

diseases.name: Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA)
diseases.definition: Microcytic, hypochromic anemia caused by inadequate total body iron stores to support erythropoiesis.
common_symptoms: Exertional fatigue and general pallor (pale conjunctiva and nail beds)
Shortness of breath on mild exertion
Dizziness, lightheadedness, and cephalalgia
Cold hands and feet
Brittle spoon-shaped nails (koilonychia) and pica (craving ice/dirt)
risk_factors: Menstruating and pregnant women
Chronic occult gastrointestinal blood loss (ulcers, polyps, colorectal lesions)
Vegetarian or vegan diets lacking bioavailable heme iron
Malabsorption syndromes (Celiac disease, post-gastric bypass)
emergency_red_flags: Severe acute anemia: Hemoglobin < 7.0 g/dL accompanied by hemodynamic instability, chest pain (angina pectoris), syncope, or resting dyspnea
Urgent blood transfusion and hospital admission required.
clinical_management: Oral iron salts (Ferrous sulfate / fumarate / bisglycinate) taken with Vitamin C
Intravenous iron sucrose/carboxymaltose for refractory cases or severe malabsorption
Mandatory diagnostic workup for gastrointestinal source in adult males and postmenopausal females

diseases.name: Vitamin B12 Deficiency
diseases.definition: A nutritional deficiency of cobalamin essential for DNA synthesis and myelin sheath integrity, resulting in megaloblastic anemia and irreversible neuropathy.

clinical_thresholds.mcv: > 100 fL (macrocytosis, often present but can be masked by concurrent iron deficiency)

common_symptoms: Peripheral neuropathy: symmetrical numbness, tingling, or 'pins and needles' in hands and feet
Subacute combined degeneration: gait ataxia, loss of proprioception and vibratory sense
Glossitis (smooth, beefy red tongue)
Megaloblastic anemia fatigue and pale jaundice (lemon-yellow skin hue)
Neuropsychiatric symptoms: memory loss, confusion, paranoia, depression
risk_factors: Strict vegan or vegetarian diets without supplementation
Pernicious anemia (anti-intrinsic factor antibodies)
Chronic Metformin or Proton Pump Inhibitor (PPI) pharmacotherapy
Atrophic gastritis and elderly age
emergency_red_flags: Acute ataxia, inability to walk, severe confusion, or progressive motor paresis
Irreversible neurological damage occurs if B12 treatment is delayed.
clinical_management: Intramuscular cyanocobalamin / hydroxocobalamin injections (1000 mcg)
High-dose oral cobalamin (1000-2000 mcg/day) for maintenance
Never administer folate alone before ruling out B12 deficiency (prevents subacute cord degeneration mask)

diseases.name: Folate (Vitamin B9) Deficiency
diseases.definition: Depletion of body folate stores required for one-carbon metabolism, RNA/DNA synthesis, and red blood cell maturation.

clinical_thresholds.clinical_note: Associated with elevated homocysteine but normal methylmalonic acid (MMA).

common_symptoms: Megaloblastic anemia symptoms: severe exhaustion, pallor, shortness of breath
Oral aphthous ulcers and sore tongue (stomatitis)
Mild gastrointestinal disturbances and weight loss
Unlike B12 deficiency, prominent peripheral sensory neuropathy is ABSENT.
risk_factors: Insufficient intake of leafy greens, citrus, and fortified grains
Chronic alcohol use disorder (inhibits enterohepatic circulation)
Pregnancy and lactation (dramatically increased fetal neural tube demands)
Antifolate medications (Methotrexate, Trimethoprim, Phenytoin)
emergency_red_flags: Neural tube defect risk (spina bifida / anencephaly) in pregnant mothers with severe deficiency
Critical severe anemia requiring blood product resuscitation
clinical_management: Oral folic acid supplementation: 1 - 5 mg daily
Dietary counseling: dark leafy greens (spinach, kale), legumes, citrus fruits
Mandatory 400 - 800 mcg/day periconceptional supplementation for women of childbearing age

diseases.name: Vitamin D Deficiency
diseases.definition: Insufficient circulating levels of 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D], impairing intestinal calcium/phosphate absorption and bone mineral homeostasis.
common_symptoms: Diffuse bone pain and skeletal tenderness (especially ribs, hips, tibia)
Proximal muscle weakness and difficulty climbing stairs or standing from chairs
Increased susceptibility to respiratory tract infections
Chronic bone loss, osteoporosis, and fragility fractures in adults; rickets in children
risk_factors: Limited sunlight exposure (high latitude, indoor occupations, sun-protective clothing)
Deeply pigmented skin (melanin absorbs UV-B photons)
Obesity (BMI > 30 kg/m², sequestration in adipose stores)
Chronic kidney or liver disease (impaired 1-alpha-hydroxylation)
emergency_red_flags: Severe hypocalcemia secondary to profound deficiency: tetany, laryngospasm, carpopedal spasms, cardiac QT-prolongation and ventricular arrhythmias
Immediate IV calcium gluconate and telemetry required.
clinical_management: High-dose ergocalciferol (Vitamin D2) or cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3): 50,000 IU weekly for 8 weeks
Maintenance therapy: 1,500 - 2,000 IU daily
Adequate elemental calcium intake (1,000 - 1,200 mg daily)
